title: Address is fully unstructured
msg: PstlAdr has AdrLine only - no TwnNm and no Ctry. A fully unstructured address is the one shape CBPR+ removes; every agent on the route has to repair it by hand.
cite: SWIFT CBPR+ Usage Guidelines, PostalAddress24 - fully unstructured addresses withdrawn at the SR 2026 cutover (deferred 2026-08-27, revised timetable due by December 2026).

title: Ctry missing
msg: PstlAdr has structured fields but no <Ctry>. Country is mandatory in both the structured and the hybrid address option.
cite: ISO 20022 PostalAddress24 - Ctry mandatory for in-scope agents and parties under CBPR+.

title: TwnNm missing in a hybrid address
msg: PstlAdr mixes AdrLine with structured fields but has no <TwnNm>. Town and Country are the minimum a hybrid address must populate.
cite: SWIFT CBPR+ hybrid postal address, live since 2025-11-22 - TwnNm plus Ctry required at minimum.

title: Structured value repeated inside AdrLine
msg: A value that already sits in a dedicated element is repeated inside an AdrLine. That is not a compliant hybrid address, it is malformed, and it may be rejected rather than repaired.
cite: SWIFT CBPR+ hybrid rule - if a component has a dedicated structured field it must go there and must not also appear in AdrLine.

title: More than two AdrLine occurrences
msg: The hybrid postal address option allows at most two AdrLine occurrences. Extra lines are dropped or the message is rejected.
cite: SWIFT CBPR+ Usage Guidelines - AdrLine limited to 2 occurrences in the hybrid option.

title: Ctry is not an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code
msg: <Ctry> must be exactly two upper-case letters. A country name or a three-letter code fails schema validation before the payment ever leaves.

title: AdrLine longer than 70 characters
msg: AdrLine is Max70Text. Anything past character 70 is truncated on the wire, and a truncated beneficiary address is a sanctions-screening hit waiting to happen.

title: Character outside the CBPR+ character set
msg: An address field carries a character outside the permitted SWIFT set (letters, digits and / - ? : ( ) . , ' + space). Ampersands and accented letters are the usual cause of a NAK or a silent substitution.
cite: SWIFT CBPR+ character set restriction on ISO 20022 text elements.

title: House number buried in StrtNm
msg: StrtNm carries the house number and no <BldgNb> is present. The structured option has a dedicated element for it; leaving it in the street name is what makes address matching fail downstream.
cite: ISO 20022 PostalAddress24 - BldgNb is the dedicated element for the building number.
